name: Home controls
summary: Smart home controls: rooms as chips, and device tiles that switch on and off, with a brightness slider for lights, a dial-like thermostat stepper, a lock and a speaker with volume.
use: in a smart home app's main screen, for switching lights, heating, locks and speakers room by room
a11y: Rooms are a radio group; each device is a toggle button with aria-pressed whose name reads the device and its state, sliders are named range inputs, and the thermostat buttons say the temperature they will set.

use_when: a handful of on-off devices grouped by room, where a few also need one level such as brightness, volume or a target temperature
avoid_when: app or account preferences rather than physical devices: use settings-toggles
one device in depth with schedules and history: use detail-drawer
a single media player with a queue: use music-player

parts.name: title
parts.what: the home's name, the section heading

parts.name: summary
parts.what: a one-line status; the active count updates as devices switch

parts.name: rooms
parts.what: one room chip with its device count; the chips filter the tiles

parts.name: devices
parts.what: one device tile; on tiles are raised and their icon is accented

parts.name: toggle
parts.what: the tile's switch: icon, device name and its current state

parts.name: level
parts.what: an optional slider for brightness or volume

parts.name: thermostat
parts.what: a wide tile with a dial showing the target temperature, its name and room, and lower and raise buttons

parts.name: target
parts.what: the target temperature and the heating mode

parts.name: steppers
parts.what: lower and raise the target by half a degree

empty.how: for a room with no devices, hide the tile grid and show empty-state ('No devices in this room yet') with an Add device button

loading.how: keep the room chips and draw each tile as a sunken box with muted blocks for the icon, name and state

error.how: when a device does not respond, put its toggle back, write 'Not responding' in its state line and add an alert-banners notice above the tiles

disabled.how: the thermostat's lower and raise buttons disable at the minimum and maximum, in the disabled colour

overflow.how: room chips scroll sideways in their own row with a fade at the edge; tiles go to 3 or 4 columns as the box widens

long_text.how: the state line ends in an ellipsis; room chips never wrap and device names wrap inside the tile
long_text.evidence: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis

keyboard: Tab reaches the room chips as one radio group; the arrow keys move between rooms and filter the tiles
Tab then reaches each device toggle; Enter or Space switches it on or off
On a brightness or volume slider, the arrow keys, Home and End change the level
On the thermostat, Enter or Space on Lower or Raise changes the target by half a degree; each button is disabled at its limit
